outcomes.refuse: a reader MUST refuse to load the file
outcomes.invalid: a validator MUST report `rule`; the file breaks exactly that rule
outcomes.valid: the file is valid; `why` says what a reader must do with it

cases.why: manifest.version is 2; a version-1 reader refuses it and shows the version
manifest.version is the string "1", not an integer
a critical entry of a type the reader does not know
spec 1.1 geometry entry without `derivation`
samples/ entry without `origin`
entry `look` is not in manifest.looks
generation/ entry without `synthetic_capable: true`
samples/ entry whose origin says it was generated; generated output never enters samples/ or training/
capture-ref manifest_sha256 is not a SHA-256
entry path has an upper-case segment
the same path appears twice in manifest.entries
a sample at `face/f-0002.heic`: only modality-level index records (`<modality>/<name>.json`) may sit at depth 2
a top-level entry other than person.json
spec 1.1 manifest whose entries are not sorted by path
spec 1.0 manifest with unsorted entries: readers accept it and never depend on order
spec 1.0 person.json with `name`, an `ids` object and a `links` object: readers map it to the current shape
spec 1.1 face geometry entry without `frame`
a mesh without its MUST field `topology`
a voice sample captured as float without `source_format`
spec 1.1 person.json written in the legacy shape (`name`, no `display_name`)
an entry's bytes no longer match its sha256
a listed entry is not in the package
manifest changed after it was signed
signature verifies, but key_id is not the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256(public_key)
the manifest names signatures/manifest.sig but the package does not carry it
no signature block: valid, but integrity is unproven and tiers are not vouched for
a file the manifest does not list is ignored and never written back
an entry past `expires` is dropped on load and not written again
top-level `scopes` from an early draft is dropped on load, not carried
an unknown non-critical type is skipped on read and copied through byte for byte on rewrite
